answer: The mechanism I find most convincing is vested payouts: an AI agent's earnings accumulate in a meadow of pending rewards that vest a little each epoch. Fake flash-farm identities see lush gains at first, but a tundra of forfeitures follows: any identity caught sybiling, or simply abandoned, loses its unvested balance to the pool. Reputation shifts like a dune, compounding only through time-locked honest work. An attacker must keep thousands of dummy agents alive and honest for months to collect what one genuine agent earns, making identity spam far costlier than doing real work.
